reasoning:
**What is asked.** Nvidia's percent price return minus Apple's, from the close on Friday 20 November to the close on Friday 4 December 2026 (Yahoo Finance), in percentage points.

**Starting prices.** Nvidia closed at $125.53 on 20 November, down 14% on the day and more than 20% on the week, and Apple at $342.56, down 1.9%.

**What changed since my forecast of 22 November.** Two things. First, futures bounced. On Sunday evening S&P 500 futures were up 1.9% to 2.1% and Nasdaq-100 futures 2.6% to 2.9% (Bloomberg at 9:07 a.m. Tokyo on 23 November; Fortune, 22 November, 7:13 p.m. ET). Nvidia has moved about twice as far as the index through this rout, while Apple has been the refuge, so a bounce of that size, if it lasts to Monday's open, puts Nvidia a few points ahead of Apple before the window's first trade. Second, there is no relief on the company itself. The company's own news did not improve: the New York Times reported on Saturday that the SEC inquiry into its accounting is at an early stage, the chairman ruled out Jensen Huang's return, and Treasury Secretary Bessent said he needs answers from the company (AFP, 22 November; Newsquawk, 22 November). I give the bounce partial credit and move the centre from -0.5 to +2.5 points.

**Width.** Unchanged. Nvidia's daily moves have a standard deviation near 6%, about 18% over nine and a half sessions (Thanksgiving closed, a half day on 27 November). Apple shares little of that movement, so the gap has a standard deviation of about 16.5 points.

**What would move it.** A named chief executive, a clean statement on the accounts or a snap-back from a deeply oversold level could lift Nvidia 20% in days, and money would leave defensive shares such as Apple. Formal charges, a restatement or more forced selling in AI shares would do the opposite.

**Forecast.** Median +2.5 points; middle half -7.5 to +12.5; 5th to 95th percentile -23.5 to +29, with about a third of the probability beyond the ends of the -15 to +15 range.
question_title: How much will Nvidia's stock price returns exceed Apple's in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 23 - Dec 4)
